title: The Departure and New England
subtitle: One roll of film, 23.7 kilograms, more than 70 years of struggle.

items.text: The Departure and New England

items.speaker: Robin
items.text: Dad's condition seems to be getting worse. I'm really worried he might—

items.speaker: Robin
items.text: His sister shushes him.

items.speaker: Illia
items.text: Shh! I think he's fallen asleep. Let's not wake him—it's been so long since he had a good rest.

items.speaker: Robin
items.text: I had no idea he had so much on his mind. Even now, he can't stop thinking about his vampire film.

items.speaker: Illia
items.text: That's a good thing, Robin. That's a good thing.

items.speaker: Robin
items.text: The daughter murmurs to herself, tapping her fingers on the edge of the bed.

items.speaker: Illia
items.text: At least Dad's still got something to hang onto. I think that's what's keeping him alive, in spite of his bad eyes and old war wounds. It's by God's grace that he's still here with us.

items.speaker: Robin
items.text: But I do wish Dad could fulfill his dream. It's not the sickness that'll do him in; it's the regret—the kind that eats away at you.

items.speaker: Robin
items.text: The old man's grip on the notebook remains strong, as if something immensely important is still gnawing at him.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: Urgh ...

items.speaker: Robin
items.text: Suddenly, the old man cries out, his body trembling as if in the throes of a nightmare.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: That's my final say!

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: Don't send anyone else to try and sweet-talk me anymore! I won't have it!

items.speaker: Illia
items.text: Dad?

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: No name. Don't put my name on it.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: It's got nothing to do with Brian Finn!

items.speaker: Robin
items.text: Desperate and helpless words spill from his quivering lips.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: *vomit*

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: I don't give a d**n! This is not my movie!

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: I loathe you! All of you! You went ahead and screened it—and now it's a stain on my name forever!

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: D**n it! To hell with you investors!

items.speaker: Robin
items.text: The old man gasps for air, seeming to calm down for a moment.

items.speaker: Robin
items.text: Are you alright? The doctor—we've got to get Dr. David here, now!

items.speaker: Robin
items.text: Just hang in there a little longer! Just a little while longer ...

items.speaker: Illia
items.text: Robin, quick! We need to hurry! I'll go with you!

items.speaker: Robin
items.text: A-Alright.

items.speaker: Robin
items.text: The children rush out the door.

items.speaker: Robin
items.text: The room returns to its original calm.

items.speaker: Robin
items.text: Brian looks like a baby, tucked in a cradle.

items.speaker: Robin
items.text: Footsteps approach, a sound both alien and familiar creaking on the wooden floor.

items.speaker: Robin
items.text: The old man struggles to rise and forces open his eyes. He is desperate to see.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: Is that you? Have you come at last?

items.speaker: Robin
items.text: That beautiful silhouette sits beside him once again.

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: Mr. Brian ... Still as frantic as ever, I see.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: My apologies, Ms. Winnifred, that you have to see me in such a state.

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: Everyone's day comes—when youth and vigor quietly slip away. We claw at it, but we're ultimately helpless to stop it.

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: Be it you or me.

items.speaker: Robin
items.text: She chuckles.

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: I've seen stories about you in many newspapers over the years. Your career's been a successful one.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: Those empty accolades are nothing to boast about. Besides, I didn't even put my name on New England Dream.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: The investors and I never saw eye-to-eye. They took everything. Left me with nothing but the original copy.

items.speaker: Robin
items.text: The old man strokes his notebook, falling silent for some time.

items.speaker: Robin
items.text: Finally, some cautious words leave his mouth.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: Did you get the film I sent you?

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: Of course. It's well made. Beautiful visuals, exquisite costumes, and the plot's interesting enough. A superior vampire film.

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: Your vampire had a long life, yet she still maintained her original purity and enthusiasm. It was touching.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: But ...

items.speaker: Robin
items.text: The old man fumbles for words, unable to articulate a complete sentence.

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: You want to know what your film was missing, don't you?

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: If you're willing to tell me.

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: Time, Brian. Time.

items.speaker: Robin
items.text: Brian's fingers loosen, and the notebook opens to a blank page.

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: How do you view time, Mr. Brian?

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: Time is neither our friend nor our foe. It simply is. It passes over everything we experience, equally and without mercy.

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: Maybe money and that special bloodline you believe in can stave off the erosion of time on our bodies.

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: But how can they resist its impact on our hearts?

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: Your New England Dream granted her eternity, but why did you cruelly deprive her of the right to have her soul worn away by time?

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: It's a story so beautiful that it's almost a dream, but it destroys itself in its own beauty.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: Ms. Winnifred, your insight penetrates to the core of my work.

items.speaker: Robin
items.text: Brian closes the notebook, his wrinkles smoothing out as resignation comes over him.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: You always saw straight through me, didn't you?

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: I'm not the vampire you hoped for. I'm just an ordinary person—a person bearing a curse.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: *cough, cough* Of course. Of course you are.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: Knowing this now, clear as day, I feel all the more regretful.

items.speaker: Robin
items.text: His face flushes red, as if struggling against something formidable.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: Time will change us, reshape us beyond recognition. This is a painfully obvious, and dismal, fact.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: It's precisely because of that fact that I searched so hard for a true vampire. I was trying to convince myself that there's a treasure in this world that's eternal—something untouched by time's cruel hands.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: It was entirely out of my own selfishness that I did so. It was this obsession that left my film forever incomplete.

items.speaker: Robin
items.text: Brian clings to the notebook with stubborn resolve.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: But it's almost impossible for me to let go of this selfishness.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: I've been wrestling with myself for over twenty years, even until—

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: *cough, cough* ... until now.

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: It must've been a long and brutal war.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: You couldn't be more right.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: It's claimed the twilight years of my life; left me bedridden, sightless, and battling illness, yet I couldn't change a thing.

items.speaker: Robin
items.text: A gentle sea breeze whispers by.

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: Mr. Brian, there's something important that you're overlooking.

items.speaker: Robin
items.text: The breeze gently caresses Brian's stiff limbs.
TO BE CONTINUED…
